## Description
Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR): Instruments like RIMFAX on the Perseverance &#10;&#9;&#9;rover operate at high frequencies (150 MHz–1200 MHz) to map shallow stratified structures &#10;&#9;&#9;and detect water ice or geological subsurface features, though they have limited depth &#10;&#9;&#9;penetration compared to electromagnetic methods.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;RIMFAX is a gated Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar — fundamentally &#10;&#9;&#9;different from the short-pulse GPR systems common on Earth. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;All three modes are collected every 5–10 cm along the rover&#39;s traverse, building up a &#10;&#9;&#9;2D radargram (cross-section image) of the subsurface.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;- Surface Mode:&#9;675 MHz. ~0 to 1 m Depth Range. ~10 cm Vertical Resolution.&#10;&#9;&#9;- Shallow Mode:&#9;675 MHz. ~1 to 5 m Depth Range. 10-20 cm Vertical Resolution. &#10;&#9;&#9;- Deep Mode:&#9;375 MHz. up to 10m (33 ft) Depth Range. 20-40 cm Vertical Resolution. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;What It Can Detect:&#10;&#9;&#9;- Layered geology (parallel reflectors &#61; sedimentary beds or lava flows)&#10;&#9;&#9;- Buried boulders / point scatterers (hyperbolic diffraction signatures)&#10;&#9;&#9;- Water ice or brine (higher permittivity → different velocity and stronger reflection)&#10;&#9;&#9;- Unconformities and truncations (structural discontinuities)&#10;&#9;&#9;- Surface property changes over time (diurnal cycle passive mode, with Tx off, &#10;&#9;&#9;  measuring surface reflection coefficient shifts) &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;In essence, RIMFAX is the radar equivalent of what DAN does with neutrons — it &quot;sees&quot; &#10;&#9;&#9;subsurface structure — but it does so with centimeter-scale spatial resolution and the &#10;&#9;&#9;ability to distinguish geologic layering, not just bulk hydrogen content.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;
